newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian average lending rate rose to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian average lending rate rose to 11.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 11.3 percent in intensive trade on Monday, after last week's national holiday created a shortage of kuna funds, dealer said.

The day's trade totalled 74.7 million kuna. Most of it, 42.7 million, was call money granted at a steady 10.5 percent. Neither demand nor supply were fully met as bids could not be matched due to bank lending regulations.

The weighted rate was pushed up to 11.3 from last Thursday's 10.8 percent due to an increase in term borrowings which are Term rates ranged between 9.4 percent for under five day funds to 18 percent for one 31-to-365 day loan.
Insurers prolonged seven-day funds at nine percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday weaker at 6.1278 aganst the dollar and firmer at 3.5664 against the mark -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
